# Modular Portable Dusty Air Cleaner: System Description

## Overview

The modular portable dusty air cleaner is a self-contained filtration system engineered for efficient particulate removal from contaminated air streams. Its architecture comprises several integrated components: a removable bin, a dirty gas distributor, an aperture plate, multiple tubular filters, a roof, a clean-gas chamber, a dust collection chamber, and a pulse-jet assembly. Together, these elements form a cohesive unit designed for effective dust separation, filtration, and cleaning, while also supporting ease of maintenance and dust disposal.

## Dirty Gas Distribution

Central to the operation of the system is the dirty gas distributor, which is strategically positioned to introduce contaminated air into the dust collection chamber. This distributor directs the incoming dirty gas toward the periphery of the tubular filters rather than directly at their surfaces. This peripheral introduction promotes a more uniform distribution of airflow around the filters, reducing localized turbulence and uneven particulate loading. By allowing the dirty gas to enter from the outer boundary of the filter arrangement, the design encourages a more gradual and controlled migration of air toward the filter media, which can help minimize premature clogging and improve overall filtration efficiency.

## Aperture Plate and Filter Configuration

The aperture plate plays a dual structural and functional role within the system. It serves as at least a partial ceiling for the removable bin, effectively separating the lower dust collection region from the upper portions of the assembly. Each tubular filter is suspended from this plate, extending downward into the bin through a dedicated aperture. This configuration ensures that every filter is individually seated and supported, allowing for consistent alignment and stable operation. The arrangement of multiple apertures, each corresponding to a single filter, facilitates a modular design in which filters can be inspected, serviced, or replaced with relative ease, without disrupting the integrity of the surrounding structure.

## Clean-Gas Chamber and Housing

Above the aperture plate lies the roof, which together with the plate defines the boundaries of the clean-gas chamber. This chamber occupies the space between the top surface of the aperture plate and the underside of the roof, and it serves as the primary reservoir for air that has already passed through the tubular filters and been cleaned of particulate matter. Importantly, the clean-gas chamber also houses the pulse-jet assembly, integrating the cleaning mechanism directly into the pathway of the filtered air stream. This placement allows the pulse-jet components to interface efficiently with each filter from above, ensuring that cleaning pulses can be delivered directly down through the length of each tubular element.

## Pulse-Jet Cleaning Mechanism

The pulse-jet assembly is responsible for maintaining the ongoing performance of the tubular filters by periodically dislodging accumulated dust from their surfaces. This assembly incorporates a set of nozzles, with one nozzle dedicated to each individual filter. During operation, the nozzles emit short, high-pressure pulses of gas that travel downward through the interior of each filter. This reverse-flow pulsing action disrupts the dust cake that has built up on the exterior of the filter media, causing the accumulated particulate matter to detach and fall away. The dislodged dust then descends into the bottom of the dust collection chamber, where it can be gathered and subsequently removed via the removable bin. This pulse-cleaning process allows the system to sustain effective filtration performance over extended periods of use, reducing the frequency of manual maintenance while preserving consistent airflow and filtration quality throughout the operational cycle.

## Integrated System Function

Taken together, these components form a coordinated system in which dirty air enters through the distributor, passes through the tubular filters for particulate removal, and exits into the clean-gas chamber as purified air. Simultaneously, the pulse-jet assembly ensures the filters remain functional over time by periodically clearing accumulated dust into the collection chamber below, from which it can be conveniently disposed of via the removable bin. This modular, portable design allows for flexible deployment in various industrial or environmental settings requiring reliable air purification.

# Modular Portable Dusty Air Cleaner

## Field of the Invention

This invention relates to air filtration systems, and more particularly to a modular, portable dust collection apparatus incorporating pulse-jet self-cleaning technology for efficient removal of particulate matter from contaminated air streams.

## Background

Industrial and commercial environments frequently generate dust-laden air that requires filtration before being released into the atmosphere or recirculated into a workspace. Traditional dust collection systems are often large, stationary installations that are difficult to relocate, service, or scale according to changing operational needs. Furthermore, conventional filter systems typically require manual cleaning or filter replacement, resulting in downtime and increased maintenance costs. There exists a need for a compact, portable dust collector that can maintain high filtration efficiency while minimizing manual intervention through automated self-cleaning mechanisms.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a modular portable dusty air cleaner designed to efficiently capture, filter, and periodically self-clean particulate contaminants from an air stream. The apparatus comprises several key structural components working in concert to achieve continuous, low-maintenance filtration performance in a compact footprint suitable for portability.

### Removable Collection Bin

At the base of the apparatus is a removable bin that serves as the primary dust collection chamber. This bin is designed for easy detachment from the main housing, allowing operators to conveniently empty accumulated dust without disassembling the entire unit. The removable nature of the bin also facilitates transport of the collected particulate matter and simplifies routine maintenance procedures.

### Dirty Gas Distributor

Positioned above the collection bin, the dirty gas distributor receives the incoming contaminated air stream and directs its flow evenly across the filtration elements. This component ensures uniform air distribution, preventing localized overloading of individual filters and promoting balanced filtration across the entire filter bank, thereby extending filter life and maintaining consistent performance.

### Aperture Plate with Tubular Filters

A critical structural element of the system is the aperture plate, which contains a series of openings from which tubular filters are suspended in a hanging configuration. These cylindrical filter elements provide substantial surface area for capturing airborne particulates as the dirty air passes through them from the outside inward (or as configured). The hanging arrangement allows dust cake to build up on the filter surfaces during normal operation while facilitating effective dislodgement during the cleaning cycle.

### Clean-Gas Chamber

Above the aperture plate and filter assembly lies the clean-gas chamber, which collects the filtered air after it has passed through the tubular filters. This chamber serves as a plenum from which the purified air is subsequently exhausted from the unit or routed for further use, ensuring that only properly filtered air exits the system.

### Pulse-Jet Cleaning Assembly

Integrated into the clean-gas chamber is a pulse-jet assembly featuring individual nozzles corresponding to each tubular filter element. This assembly is the key self-cleaning mechanism of the invention. At programmed or sensor-triggered intervals, the pulse-jet system delivers a short, high-pressure burst of compressed air through each nozzle in a reverse direction relative to normal airflow. This reverse pulse rapidly expands the filter media and creates a shockwave that dislodges the accumulated dust cake adhering to the exterior surface of each tubular filter.

## Operation

During normal operation, dust-laden air enters through the dirty gas distributor and flows around and through the hanging tubular filters mounted on the aperture plate. As air passes through the filter media, particulate matter is captured on the outer surface of the filters, while cleaned air continues upward into the clean-gas chamber and exits the unit.

Over time, as dust accumulates on the filter surfaces, pressure differential across the filters increases. When cleaning is initiated—either through a timed sequence or in response to a pressure differential sensor—the pulse-jet assembly fires a rapid burst of compressed air through the nozzle corresponding to each filter, in sequence or simultaneously. This reverse-flow pulse causes the filter media to flex outward momentarily, breaking the adhesion of the collected dust cake and causing it to fall by gravity into the removable collection bin positioned below.

This self-cleaning cycle can be repeated automatically at regular intervals, ensuring that filter efficiency and airflow capacity are continuously restored without requiring manual intervention or system shutdown. The dislodged dust settles into the bin, which can be periodically removed and emptied by the operator.

## Advantages

The modular design of this dusty air cleaner offers several advantages over conventional systems:

1. **Portability**: The compact configuration allows the unit to be easily relocated between work sites or repositioned within a facility as needed.

2. **Self-Cleaning Operation**: The pulse-jet assembly eliminates the need for manual filter cleaning, reducing labor costs and minimizing system downtime.

3. **Modularity**: Individual components—including the filters, aperture plate, and collection bin—can be independently serviced, replaced, or reconfigured, simplifying maintenance and extending the operational life of the unit.

4. **Efficient Dust Removal**: The combination of gravity-assisted dust settling and the removable bin design allows for quick and clean disposal of collected particulates.

5. **Continuous Operation**: Because cleaning cycles can occur without interrupting airflow, the system supports uninterrupted operation in continuous-duty applications.

## Conclusion

This invention provides a practical and efficient solution to the challenges of industrial air filtration through a modular, self-cleaning, and portable design. By integrating a removable collection bin, a dirty gas distributor, an aperture plate with hanging tubular filters, a clean-gas chamber, and a corresponding pulse-jet cleaning assembly, the apparatus achieves high filtration performance while significantly reducing maintenance requirements. The result is a versatile air cleaning system suitable for a wide range of industrial, commercial, and field applications where portability and low-maintenance operation are essential.

# Patent Claim Summary

## Portable Industrial Dust Collector with Pulse-Jet Cleaning System

**Field of Invention:** This invention relates to portable dust collection systems, and more particularly to a mobile industrial dust collector employing pulse-jet cleaning technology for tubular filter elements.

---

### Claim 1 (Independent)

A portable industrial dust collector comprising:

(a) a mobile housing assembly mounted on a wheeled chassis, said housing defining a dirty air inlet plenum and a clean air outlet plenum;

(b) a plurality of tubular filter elements disposed vertically within said housing, each filter element having a closed bottom end, an open top end, and a perforated support cage extending along its interior length;

(c) a tube sheet separating said dirty air inlet plenum from said clean air outlet plenum, wherein said tubular filter elements are mounted through apertures in said tube sheet with the open top ends extending into a clean air chamber;

(d) a pulse-jet cleaning system comprising:
   (i) a compressed air manifold positioned above said tube sheet,
   (ii) a plurality of blow pipes fluidly connected to said manifold, each blow pipe having a series of orifices aligned coaxially with the open ends of said tubular filter elements,
   (iii) a plurality of solenoid-actuated diaphragm valves interposed between said manifold and said blow pipes,
   (iv) a programmable timer/controller configured to sequentially actuate said diaphragm valves to discharge short-duration compressed air pulses into said tubular filter elements in a reverse-flow direction relative to normal filtration airflow;

(e) an induced-draft fan in fluid communication with said clean air outlet plenum for drawing contaminated air through said dirty air inlet and through the filter media of said tubular filter elements;

(f) a dust collection hopper disposed beneath said dirty air inlet plenum for receiving dislodged particulate matter during the cleaning cycle; and

(g) a caster-equipped or wheeled base frame supporting said housing, hopper, fan, and cleaning system as an integrated, self-contained, transportable unit.

---

### Claim 2 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, wherein said programmable timer/controller further comprises a differential pressure sensor configured to monitor pressure drop across said tubular filter elements and to initiate said pulse-jet cleaning sequence automatically when a predetermined pressure differential threshold is exceeded.

### Claim 3 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, wherein each of said tubular filter elements comprises a pleated filter media selected from the group consisting of spun-bond polyester, cellulose blend, and PTFE-membrane laminate.

### Claim 4 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, wherein said compressed air manifold is supplied by an onboard compressed air reservoir tank mounted to said base frame, enabling operation independent of facility compressed air infrastructure.

### Claim 5 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, further comprising a quick-disconnect duct coupling on said dirty air inlet plenum for rapid connection to a source-capture hood or ducted process exhaust.

### Claim 6 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, wherein said hopper includes a removable, sealable collection drum disposed on a slide-out tray for ease of dust disposal without interrupting the filtration process.

### Claim 7 (Dependent)

The dust collector of claim 1, wherein said pulse-jet cleaning system is configured to clean said tubular filter elements in a row-by-row or bank-by-bank sequence to maintain continuous filtration capacity during online cleaning.

### Claim 8 (Independent — Method Claim)

A method of collecting and cleaning particulate-laden air using a portable pulse-jet dust collector, comprising:

(a) drawing contaminated air through a dirty air inlet into contact with the exterior surfaces of a plurality of vertically mounted tubular filter elements via an induced-draft fan;
(b) accumulating filtered particulate on the exterior surfaces of said tubular filter elements while clean air passes through said filter media into a clean air plenum;
(c) monitoring differential pressure across said tubular filter elements via a pressure sensor;
(d) upon detecting a pressure differential exceeding a predetermined threshold, sequentially actuating diaphragm valves to discharge pulses of compressed air into the interior of said tubular filter elements in a direction opposite to normal filtration flow, thereby dislodging accumulated dust cake from said exterior surfaces; and
(e) collecting said dislodged particulate in a hopper disposed beneath said tubular filter elements, wherein steps (a)–(e) are performed within a single wheeled, self-contained housing transportable between work locations.

---

**Note:** The above claims are illustrative in nature. Additional dependent claims may be drafted to cover specific structural variations (e.g., filter cartridge quick-release mechanisms, HEPA after-filter stages, spark-arrestor inlet screens, explosion venting panels, variable-frequency fan drives, or battery/solar-powered control systems) depending on the specific embodiments disclosed in the full specification and drawings.

counterfactuals.output:
# Modular Pulse-Jet Air Cleaner with Removable Dust Bin Assembly

## System Overview

This design describes a modular industrial air filtration system employing pulse-jet cleaning technology to maintain cartridge filter efficiency through automated, reverse-pulse cleaning cycles. The system integrates a removable dust collection bin, a structural aperture plate, and a bank of pulse-jet nozzles into a unified housing designed for high dust-load applications such as welding fume extraction, powder handling, and pneumatic conveying exhaust.

## Core Components

### 1. Housing and Filtration Chamber

The main housing is divided into two chambers separated by a tube sheet (aperture plate):

- **Dirty air plenum** (lower/inlet chamber): Receives contaminated airflow and houses the cartridge filters
- **Clean air plenum** (upper/outlet chamber): Receives filtered air prior to discharge or recirculation

Dust-laden air enters tangentially or axially into the dirty air plenum, promoting inertial separation of coarse particulate before contact with filter media.

### 2. Aperture Plate (Tube Sheet)

The aperture plate is a rigid, gasketed dividing wall that:

- Provides structural mounting points for the filter cartridges via threaded studs, cam-lock mechanisms, or venturi-seated openings
- Maintains an airtight seal between clean and dirty air plenums, preventing bypass of unfiltered air
- Contains precision-machined apertures sized to match cartridge open-face diameter and to accommodate the venturi inserts used during pulse cleaning
- Is typically constructed from powder-coated or galvanized steel, with gasket seating surfaces to accept cartridge door or flange seals

### 3. Cartridge Filters

Pleated media cartridges (commonly polyester, cellulose, or PTFE-membrane laminate) are mounted vertically or horizontally through the aperture plate openings. Airflow passes from outside to inside the pleats, depositing dust on the exterior media surface while allowing clean air to exit through the cartridge core into the clean air plenum.

### 4. Pulse-Jet Cleaning Nozzles

A cleaning header assembly is mounted in the clean air plenum, consisting of:

- **Compressed air manifold**: Fed by a plant air supply (typically 80–100 psi), regulated and filtered
- **Diaphragm solenoid valves**: One valve typically serves one or more rows of cartridges, triggered sequentially
- **Blow pipes with drilled orifices or nozzles**: Aligned precisely over each cartridge's open core or venturi throat to direct a short-duration, high-volume air pulse (typically 80–150 milliseconds) down through the cartridge interior

The pulse creates a reverse-flow shockwave that momentarily reverses airflow through the media, flexing the pleats and dislodging the accumulated dust cake, which falls by gravity into the dust bin below.

### 5. Venturi Inserts

Positioned at the aperture plate opening above each cartridge, venturi inserts amplify the compressed air pulse by inducing secondary airflow from the clean plenum, improving cleaning energy distribution across the full cartridge length while minimizing compressed air consumption.

### 6. Removable Dust Bin

Located beneath the dirty air plenum, the dust bin is designed for tool-free removal and typically includes:

- **Slide-out or drawer-style mounting** on rails, or a bolt/latch-secured hopper with quick-release clamps
- **Gasketed interface** to the housing to prevent air infiltration/dust leakage during normal operation
- **Optional liner bag or drum interface** for direct disposal
- **Level sensors or sight glass** (optional) to indicate fill status
- **Access door interlock** (in some designs) to prevent bin removal during active fan operation, or to trigger fan shutdown for safety

## Cleaning Cycle Operation

1. A differential pressure (ΔP) transmitter continuously monitors pressure drop across the cartridge bank (typically maintaining 2–6 in. W.C.).
2. When ΔP exceeds a programmed setpoint (or on a timed interval), the controller initiates a cleaning sequence.
3. Solenoid valves fire sequentially (row-by-row) to avoid excessive compressed air demand and to maintain filtration continuity in unpulsed rows.
4. Each pulse is timed to allow re-settling of dust and diaphragm valve recharge (typically 10–30 seconds between pulses) before the next row fires.
5. Dislodged dust falls through the dirty air plenum into the removable dust bin.
6. The cycle continues until all rows are cleaned, then resets, either continuously (on/off with fan operation) or based on ΔP recovery.

## Modularity Features

- **Cartridge count scalability**: The aperture plate can be manufactured in varying sizes/hole counts to support different airflow capacities without redesigning the housing.
- **Nozzle header compatibility**: The pulse-jet manifold is indexed to the aperture plate hole pattern, allowing standardized header assemblies across multiple housing sizes.
- **Bin interchangeability**: Multiple bin configurations (drawer, drum stand, or bag-out) can be fitted to the same housing base using a common flange/seal interface.
- **Serviceability**: Cartridges, aperture plate, and nozzles can be accessed via a hinged or removable door without disturbing the dust bin, and the bin can be removed independently for waste disposal without interrupting airflow to other modules (in multi-module installations).

## Materials and Construction Considerations

- Housing: Carbon steel (painted or galvanized) or stainless steel for corrosive/food-grade applications
- Gaskets: Neoprene, silicone, or high-temperature EPDM depending on process temperature
- Aperture plate: Minimum 12–14 gauge steel for structural rigidity under pulse pressure loading
- Dust bin: Reinforced corners and rolling casters or forklift-accessible skids for heavy dust loads

## Performance Parameters (Typical)

| Parameter | Typical Range |
|---|---|
| Air-to-cloth ratio | 2:1 to 4:1 (ft³/min per ft²) |
| Pulse pressure | 80–100 psi |
| Pulse duration | 80–150 ms |
| Cleaning ΔP setpoint | 3–5 in. W.C. |
| Cartridge efficiency | 99.9%+ @ 0.5–2 microns (MERV 15–16 typical) |

---

This modular architecture allows a single core design—housing, aperture plate, and nozzle header—to be scaled across a range of airflow capacities and dust-loading applications while simplifying maintenance through independent access to filtration and waste-handling subsystems.

# Abstract

**Design and Performance Characterization of a Pulse-Jet Fabric Filter Dust Collection System with Optimized Dirty-Gas Distribution**

This paper presents the engineering design and operational analysis of an industrial dust collection system incorporating a dirty-gas inlet distributor, filter media chamber, clean-gas plenum, and automated pulse-jet cleaning mechanism. The system is engineered to remove particulate matter from process gas streams while maintaining consistent pressure differential and maximizing filter media service life.

The dirty-gas distributor is designed to achieve uniform velocity profiles and minimize direct particulate impingement on filter elements, thereby reducing localized media wear and preventing premature blinding. Contaminated gas enters the distribution chamber, where baffle geometry promotes even flow distribution across the array of filter bags or cartridges, reducing turbulence-induced re-entrainment of collected dust.

Filtration occurs as particulate-laden gas passes through the filter media, with dust cake formation on the exterior surface enhancing collection efficiency for sub-micron particles. Filtered gas migrates to the clean-gas chamber, from which it is discharged to atmosphere or recirculated to the process, depending on system configuration.

Filter regeneration is accomplished through a sequenced pulse-jet cleaning mechanism, wherein compressed air pulses—typically 90–100 psi, 100–150 millisecond duration—are discharged through venturi-equipped blow tubes into individual filter rows. This introduces a reverse shock wave that dislodges the accumulated dust cake without necessitating system shutdown, enabling continuous operation. Cleaning frequency is governed by differential pressure setpoints monitored via transmitters positioned across the dirty and clean-gas chambers, with cleaning cycles initiated on-demand or at timed intervals to balance emission compliance against compressed air consumption.

Key performance parameters evaluated include air-to-cloth ratio, pressure drop across filter media (typically maintained between 4–8 in. w.g.), pulse cleaning efficiency, and particulate emission rates at the clean-gas outlet. The system architecture demonstrates applicability across diverse industrial processes, including cement production, metal processing, grain handling, and combustion flue gas treatment, offering a robust solution for regulatory compliance with particulate emission standards while minimizing maintenance intervals and operational costs.

**Keywords:** pulse-jet filtration, baghouse dust collector, dirty-gas distribution, filter cake regeneration, particulate emission control, air-to-cloth ratio

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**Dust Collection Apparatus with Pulse-Jet Filter Cleaning Assembly**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to industrial dust collection systems, and more particularly to a filtration apparatus employing a plurality of tubular filter elements mounted to an aperture plate within a collection bin, wherein a pulse-jet assembly periodically discharges compressed air to dislodge accumulated particulate matter from exterior surfaces of the filter elements.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Industrial processes often generate particulate-laden air streams that must be filtered prior to discharge into the environment or recirculation into a workspace. Conventional dust collection systems typically employ filter bags or cartridges that progressively accumulate a dust cake on their surfaces, resulting in increased pressure drop across the filter media and reduced system efficiency over time. Periodic cleaning of the filter media is therefore necessary to maintain acceptable operational parameters.

Prior art cleaning mechanisms have suffered from various deficiencies, including uneven distribution of cleaning air pulses, inadequate dislodgement of caked particulate matter, mechanical complexity leading to increased maintenance requirements, and inefficient collection of dislodged particulate matter within the associated collection bin. There exists a need for an improved dust collection apparatus that addresses these shortcomings through a simplified yet effective construction.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a dust collection apparatus comprising a bin defining an interior collection chamber, an aperture plate disposed within or atop the bin and defining a plurality of apertures, a plurality of tubular filter elements each having a first end sealingly engaged with a corresponding aperture of the aperture plate and a second closed end extending into a filtration chamber, and a pulse-jet assembly configured to selectively discharge a burst of compressed gas into an interior volume of each tubular filter element to dislodge particulate matter accumulated on an exterior surface thereof, whereupon the dislodged particulate matter falls under gravity into the collection chamber of the bin.

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, the pulse-jet assembly comprises a compressed air manifold, a plurality of nozzles each aligned coaxially with a respective tubular filter element, and a plurality of solenoid-actuated valves controlling the discharge of compressed air from the manifold through the nozzles, the valves being actuated sequentially or simultaneously according to a predetermined cleaning cycle.

In accordance with another aspect of the invention, the aperture plate is disposed intermediate a dirty-air plenum and a clean-air plenum, such that particulate-laden air entering the dirty-air plenum passes through the tubular filter elements from the exterior toward the interior thereof, with filtered air exiting through the apertures into the clean-air plenum, while particulate matter dislodged by the pulse-jet assembly falls downward through the dirty-air plenum into the bin.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** is a perspective view of the dust collection apparatus according to an embodiment of the invention.

**FIG. 2** is a cross-sectional side view of the apparatus taken along a vertical plane, illustrating the bin, aperture plate, tubular filter elements, and pulse-jet assembly.

**FIG. 3** is a top plan view of the aperture plate showing the arrangement of apertures for receiving the tubular filter elements.

**FIG. 4** is an enlarged cross-sectional view of a single tubular filter element illustrating the pulse-jet nozzle positioned therein.

**FIG. 5** is a schematic diagram of the pulse-jet assembly control system.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Referring now to FIG. 1 and FIG. 2, the dust collection apparatus **10** comprises a bin **20** defining an interior collection chamber **22** for receiving and storing particulate matter removed from an air stream. The bin **20** includes a bottom wall **24**, a plurality of side walls **26**, and an open top **28** in communication with a filtration housing **30** disposed thereabove.

An aperture plate **40** is mounted within the filtration housing **30**, separating a dirty-air plenum **32** from a clean-air plenum **34**. The aperture plate **40** defines a plurality of apertures **42** arranged in a predetermined pattern, as shown in FIG. 3, each aperture **42** being dimensioned to sealingly receive a first open end **52** of a corresponding tubular filter element **50**.

Each tubular filter element **50** comprises a cylindrical body of filter media extending downwardly from the aperture plate **40** into the dirty-air plenum **32**, terminating in a second closed end **54** distal from the aperture plate **40**. The filter media may comprise woven or non-woven fabric, felted material, pleated synthetic media, or other filtration materials known in the art, selected according to the particulate characteristics of the intended application.

In operation, particulate-laden air is introduced into the dirty-air plenum **32** through an inlet port **36**. The air stream passes through the filter media of each tubular filter element **50** in a direction from the exterior surface toward the interior volume thereof, with particulate matter being retained on the exterior surface while filtered air passes into the interior volume of the tubular filter element **50** and thence through the corresponding aperture **42** into the clean-air plenum **34**, from which it is exhausted through an outlet port **38**.

As particulate matter accumulates on the exterior surfaces of the tubular filter elements **50**, forming a dust cake, the pressure differential across the filter media increases. To maintain filtration efficiency, a pulse-jet assembly **60** is provided for periodically dislodging the accumulated dust cake.

Referring to FIG. 4, the pulse-jet assembly **60** comprises a compressed air manifold **62** disposed above the aperture plate **40** within the clean-air plenum **34**, a plurality of nozzles **64** each extending downwardly from the manifold **62** and positioned coaxially within the interior volume of a respective tubular filter element **50**, and a plurality of solenoid-actuated valves **66** interposed between the manifold **62** and each nozzle **64**.

Referring to FIG. 5, a control system **70** is operatively coupled to the solenoid-actuated valves **66** and is configured to actuate the valves **66** according to a predetermined cleaning cycle, whereby each valve **66**, upon actuation, permits a burst of compressed air to discharge from the corresponding nozzle **64** into the interior volume of the associated tubular filter element **50**. The burst of compressed air propagates through the interior volume of the tubular filter element **50** and induces a rapid outward flexure and reverse pressure pulse across the filter media, thereby dislodging particulate matter accumulated on the exterior surface thereof. The dislodged particulate matter falls under the influence of gravity through the dirty-air plenum **32** and into the collection chamber **22** of the bin **20**.

In one embodiment, the control system **70** actuates the solenoid-actuated valves **66** sequentially, such that the tubular filter elements **50** are cleaned in a rotating or successive fashion, thereby maintaining continuous filtration capacity during the cleaning cycle. In an alternative embodiment, the control system **70** actuates a plurality or all of the solenoid-actuated valves **66** substantially simultaneously.

The control system **70** may further comprise a pressure differential sensor **72** configured to measure a pressure differential between the dirty-air plenum **32** and the clean-air plenum **34**, wherein the control system **70** initiates a cleaning cycle in response to the measured pressure differential exceeding a predetermined threshold value. Alternatively, or in addition, the control system **70** may initiate cleaning cycles according to a predetermined time interval.

The bin **20** may further comprise a removable or hinged access door **80** for periodic removal of accumulated particulate matter from the collection chamber **22**. In certain embodiments, the bin **20** further comprises a discharge valve or auger mechanism for continuous or semi-continuous removal of particulate matter therefrom.

counterfactuals.output:
# Compact Pulse-Jet Air Filtration Unit: Structural Description

## Overview

The subject apparatus relates generally to gas-solid separation equipment, and more particularly to a compact pulse-jet fabric filter unit incorporating an integrated dirty gas distribution system, a modular filter element arrangement, and a dust collection chamber configured for periodic or continuous discharge of separated particulate matter.

## General Housing Configuration

The filtration unit comprises a substantially vertically oriented housing defining an interior volume, said housing being divided into at least three functionally distinct zones: an upper clean gas plenum, an intermediate filtration chamber housing a plurality of filter elements, and a lower dust collection hopper. The housing may be fabricated from welded steel plate or an equivalent structural material suitable for withstanding the operating pressures generated during both normal filtration and pulse-cleaning cycles.

## Dirty Gas Distributor

The dirty gas distributor is disposed at or near the inlet of the filtration chamber and is configured to receive a particulate-laden gas stream from an inlet duct and to distribute said stream substantially uniformly across the cross-sectional area of the filter element arrangement, thereby minimizing localized high-velocity impingement and attendant premature wear of the filter media.

In a preferred embodiment, the dirty gas distributor comprises:

1. **An inlet plenum** in fluid communication with an external dust-laden gas source, said plenum defining an inlet aperture positioned tangentially or radially with respect to the housing axis so as to impart a cyclonic or otherwise pre-separative flow pattern to the incoming gas stream;

2. **A baffle or deflector plate** mounted downstream of the inlet aperture, configured to redirect the incoming gas flow away from direct impingement upon the filter elements and to promote gravitational settling of coarser particulate fractions into the underlying dust collection chamber prior to the gas stream's engagement with the filter media;

3. **A perforated or louvered distribution plate**, optionally disposed between the inlet plenum and the filter chamber, having a plurality of apertures sized and arranged to equalize the gas velocity profile across the filter element arrangement.

The dirty gas distributor thereby serves the dual function of (a) reducing the particulate loading directly incident upon the filter media, and (b) extending the operational interval between successive pulse-cleaning cycles by virtue of said pre-separation effect.

## Filter Element Arrangement

The filter element arrangement is disposed within the intermediate filtration chamber and comprises a plurality of filter elements, which may be configured as cylindrical bags, pleated cartridges, or a combination thereof, each filter element being:

1. Mounted in a substantially vertical orientation upon a tube sheet or cell plate that structurally separates the filtration chamber from the upper clean gas plenum;

2. Open at an upper end thereof, said upper end being sealingly engaged with a corresponding aperture in the tube sheet to permit passage of filtered gas into the clean gas plenum while preventing bypass of unfiltered gas;

3. Closed at a lower end thereof, optionally supported internally by a cage or wire retainer structure configured to maintain the filter element in an expanded configuration during the filtration cycle and to resist collapse during the pulse-cleaning cycle;

4. Arranged in a regular array—for example, in rows and columns or in a circular pattern—so as to maximize the effective filtration surface area within the available housing volume, consistent with the compact form factor of the unit.

Each filter element is associated with a corresponding cleaning nozzle or venturi assembly positioned above the tube sheet and in axial alignment with the open upper end of the filter element, said nozzle being in fluid communication with a compressed air header via a quick-acting solenoid-actuated diaphragm valve.

## Pulse-Cleaning System

A compressed air manifold is mounted externally upon, or internally within, the upper clean gas plenum and comprises a plurality of diaphragm valves, each valve corresponding to a respective row or bank of filter elements. Upon actuation—whether initiated by a timer-based sequencing controller or by a differential pressure transducer monitoring the pressure drop across the filter elements—each diaphragm valve releases a short-duration, high-pressure pulse of compressed air through its associated nozzle and into the interior of the corresponding filter element(s). This reverse pulse of air propagates through the filter media, momentarily reversing the direction of gas flow therethrough and dislodging the accumulated dust cake from the exterior surface of the filter element, whereupon the dislodged particulate matter falls by gravity into the underlying dust collection chamber.

## Dust Collection Chamber

The dust collection chamber, disposed at the lower extremity of the housing, is configured as a hopper having downwardly converging walls terminating in a discharge outlet. The dust collection chamber is preferably positioned immediately beneath both the dirty gas distributor and the filter element arrangement, so as to receive: (a) coarser particulate fractions pre-separated by the dirty gas distributor, and (b) dust cake dislodged from the filter elements during the pulse-cleaning cycle.

The discharge outlet of the dust collection chamber may be equipped with a rotary airlock valve, a double-dump valve, or a slide gate valve, configured to permit periodic or continuous discharge of accumulated particulate matter without significant loss of system draft or ingress of ambient air into the housing interior.

In certain embodiments, the dust collection chamber further comprises a level sensor configured to detect an accumulation of particulate matter above a predetermined threshold and to generate a corresponding signal for actuation of the discharge outlet or for alerting an operator.

## Compactness and Integration

The compact configuration of the filtration unit is achieved through the vertical stacking and structural integration of the dirty gas distributor, filter element arrangement, and dust collection chamber within a unitary housing, thereby obviating the need for separate, spatially distributed components and associated interconnecting ductwork as are typically required in conventional filtration installations. This integrated arrangement further permits the entire unit to be assembled, transported, and installed as a single pre-fabricated module, thereby reducing on-site installation time and cost.

---

*It will be understood by those skilled in the art that the foregoing description is exemplary in nature and that various modifications may be made to the disclosed structure without departing from the scope of the invention as defined in the appended claims.*
